first_impression.reaction: Fine. It tells me in two lines what's on the page and doesn't call itself the ultimate guide. I jumped to the FAQ first like I always do, it answered plain questions plainly, so I went back and skimmed the ideas. No pricing anywhere, which for a list of craft ideas I can live with, but it means this page does nothing to answer what I actually care about with planners.

journey.quote: Not always. If guests choose their own seat at an assigned table, escort cards alone can be enough.
journey.reaction: Good. A straight answer that tells me I might not need to spend money on something. That's the opposite of an upsell and I notice it.

journey.quote: Real stone is weighty and can chip in transit; a printed version keeps the look without the luggage.
journey.reaction: Trade-offs stated honestly. More of this, less 'feels grounded'.

journey.quote: For food that doesn't carry a label, allergen declarations must be displayed in connection with the food or provided on request.
journey.reaction: Linked to FSANZ, and it says it's general information, not legal advice. That's the kind of sourcing I check and it holds up. Best paragraph on the page for me.

journey.section: How to Do Wedding Place Cards
journey.quote: Queensland guidance for events says signage needs to be clear, logical, accurate and accessible.
journey.reaction: A real government source, and I'm in Brisbane. Slightly over the top for a name card, but I'd rather that than 'experts agree'.

journey.section: How to Do Wedding Place Cards
journey.quote: If you would like someone to manage the guest list and the vendor briefings with you, start a conversation with Wedded Concierge.
journey.reaction: There it is. Halfway through a section on when to order cards, a sales pitch. Nothing on this page has shown me what Concierge costs or does yet, so this is a CTA before any evidence.

journey.section: Place Cards for a Destination Wedding
journey.quote: Agree whether that is the venue, your planner or your stylist.
journey.reaction: Useful question, but the real one is who's paying for it. If the venue already does it, I don't want a planner billing me for the same job.

journey.section: Place Cards for a Destination Wedding
journey.quote: Through Wedded Concierge, one Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact for the venue, travel, vendors and payments, and works in your time zone.
journey.reaction: 'Payments' is the word that makes me sit up. If my money goes through you to vendors, what's added on the way through? The page doesn't say.

journey.quote: Find a stationer on Wedded Marketplace, our directory of venues and vendors, and compare styles.
journey.reaction: Your directory. So do listed vendors pay to be there, and does that change what I'm quoted? Not answered. I'd cross-check any stationer I found here on Google reviews.

journey.section: Plan the table with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD and agrees the fee with you in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Fee in writing before work begins is the right thing to say. It's still not the fee model, but at least it's a commitment I can hold them to.

journey.section: Glass, Mirror and Acrylic Place Cards
journey.quote: A smooth river stone or a slice of agate with a name in metallic ink feels grounded.
journey.reaction: Filler. Doesn't bother me much, I just skip it.

unanswered_questions: Do vendors pay to be listed on Wedded Marketplace, and does Wedded Wonderland take a commission from stationers or other suppliers found there?
When a Wedded Advisor handles 'payments' to vendors, are supplier prices passed through at cost or marked up?
What is the fee model for Wedded Concierge (flat, percentage, hourly)? Even a range or a link to a fee page would do.
Is setting out place cards on the day included in a Concierge fee, or billed separately?
Is Wonderland Studio free, or is it a paid add-on?

turn_offs_found.quote: If you would like someone to manage the guest list and the vendor briefings with you, start a conversation with Wedded Concierge.
turn_offs_found.why: A CTA dropped into practical how-to content before the page has shown any evidence of what the service is or costs.

turn_offs_found.quote: Through Wedded Concierge, one Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact for the venue, travel, vendors and payments, and works in your time zone.
turn_offs_found.why: Mentions handling payments with no word on how money flows or whether supplier prices are marked up. That's exactly the catch I go looking for.

turn_offs_found.quote: A smooth river stone or a slice of agate with a name in metallic ink feels grounded.
turn_offs_found.why: Mood words instead of information. Minor.

would_share_with: My fiancée, for the ideas list and the allergen paragraph

cta_reaction.quote: Start a conversation through Wedded Concierge, and for more planning ideas, read the Wedded Wonderland magazine.
cta_reaction.why: I came for place card ideas, and the page gave me those honestly. But nothing here tells me what Concierge costs, whether you take a cut from suppliers or how payments work, and I don't enquire until those are answered on the page. I'd look for a pricing or FAQ page first.

top_3_changes: Remove the mid-article pitch from 'When to order' so the first CTA comes after the reader has had real value. Old: 'If you would like someone to manage the guest list and the vendor briefings with you, start a conversation with [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=25-unique-place-cards-for-your-wedding&utm_content=secondary).' New: '' (delete the paragraph; the destination section and closing already carry the CTA).

In 'Where to Find a Stationer', tell the reader to get pricing in writing, which costs the brand nothing and signals it isn't hiding anything. Old: 'Send each stationer your chosen idea, the setting and the final name list from your seating plan, and ask to see a sample.' New: 'Send each stationer your chosen idea, the setting and the final name list from your seating plan, and ask to see a sample and a written, itemised quote before you commit.'

In the destination checklist, make the 'who sets them out' question cover cost too, so it reads as protecting the couple from paying twice. Old: 'Agree whether that is the venue, your planner or your stylist.' New: 'Agree whether that is the venue, your planner or your stylist, and confirm in writing whether it is already included in what you are paying them.'

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction quotes an exact sentence from the draft
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ first, looking for fees, commissions and the catch
No invented brand facts; fee model, commissions, Marketplace listing terms and Studio pricing recorded as unanswered questions
Suggested edits use exact old/new strings, name no vendors and add no new facts about fees, commissions, sourcing or vetting
HTML comments and fact markers treated as invisible
Scores within 1 to 5 and top_3_changes has at most 3 items

open_questions.question: The sceptic's main blockers (Concierge fee model, Marketplace commissions, payment pass-through) are deferred by the brand for this post. Is there an existing fee or FAQ page that could be linked from the closing section without stating new facts?

assumptions: Low relevance score reflects that a sceptical groom comparing planners gets little planner-selection evidence from a place card ideas post; this is expected for the topic, not a defect.
Deleting the secondary CTA is suggested within limits; the panel chair and CRO may prefer to keep it for tracking.
